children: announced on Wednesday it has brought Nvidia's
multi-rack Vera Rubin NVL72 online, which places hundreds of Rubin GPUs into a single scale-out cluster for powering artificial intelligence.
This follows up on CoreWeave's revelation in early June that it was the first AI cloud provider to bring a Vera Rubin NVL72 online.
CoreWeave shares increased 3% during early trading on Wednesday. Nvidia inched up about 1%.

"CoreWeave was the first AI cloud provider to validate and bring up a Vera Rubin NVL72, demonstrating that this advanced rack-scale architecture could operate as a reliable, high-performance cloud service," said Chen Goldberg, executive vice president of product & engineering at CoreWeave. "With multi-rack Vera Rubin, we are connecting hundreds of Rubin GPUs as a single scale-out cluster. For customers building agentic AI, that means greater scale, faster iteration, and higher productivity as models and agents continuously learn and improve."

A single Vera Rubin NVL72 rack pairs 72 Rubin GPUs with 36 Vera CPUs, NVLink 6, ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, and BlueField-4 DPUs. With multi-rack Vera Rubin NVL72, CoreWeave unifies racks of hundreds of accelerators using Nvidia's Spectrum-X Ethernet networking into a single scale-out cluster.

The Connect X-9 SuperNICs provide 1.6 Tb/s of connectivity scale-out connectivity per GPU across multiplane, multirail paths, supporting roughly 128,000 GPUs per rail in a non-blocking fabric. The modular topology allows racks to be added without redesigning the fabric at each expansion.

CoreWeave also revealed new features for CoreWeave AI Object Storage, including cross-region write acceleration and a new Archive tier. These are designed to keep necessary data closer to AI workloads. The company said the Local Object Transport Accelerator can reduce latency by as much as eight times through managed caching on each CoreWeave Kubernetes Service node.

title: CoreWeave edges up after bringing multi-rack Vera Rubin cluster online
